content.title: About
content.content: Beef soup is a classic dish made from beef, vegetables, and broth. It has a rich meaty flavor, aromatic spices, and a warming effect. Common variations include potatoes, carrots, onions, celery, and noodles.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Beef soup is one of the oldest dishes mentioned in ancient culinary texts.
Different countries have their own versions: French "bouillon de boeuf", Japanese "gyūniku suupu", and American "beef noodle soup".
Traditionally, beef is simmered for several hours to extract maximum gelatin and flavor.
Beef broth is rich in collagen, which turns into jelly when cooled.
Some cultures add sauerkraut or fermented beans to the soup for extra depth.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Beef provides high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Source of iron
items.content: Beef supplies easily absorbed heme iron, important for blood formation.

items.title: Contains zinc
items.content: Zinc supports immune function and wound healing.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: B‑vitamins in beef help convert food into energy.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: A warm broth helps maintain fluid balance, especially in cold weather.

items.title: High saturated fat
items.content: Large portions can raise cholesterol; choose lean cuts when possible.

items.title: Sodium
items.content: Broth can be salty; consider reducing added salt.

items.title: Beef allergy
items.content: Rare, but possible for individuals with meat allergies.

items.title: Contamination
items.content: Undercooked meat may harbor harmful bacteria.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve hot, garnish with fresh herbs, lemon juice, or hot sauce to taste. Pair with bread, croutons, or rice for a complete meal.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cool the soup to room temperature, then store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. For longer storage, freeze in portions for up to 2 months. Reheat to a rolling boil before serving.
